    Create an editable CTTIR v5 design

    Source: R/cttir-design.R
    hex_design.Rd

    A call without a package starts a fresh composition with a frame and name. Supplying a package explicitly loads its editable archive motif. Archive artwork can also be reused one part at a time with hex_reuse_part(). All geometry is drawn in R. Name glyphs use the bundled JetBrains Mono font.

    Usage

    hex_design(
  package = "hexmakR",
  mode = c("dark", "light", "mono"),
  layout = c("lockup", "hex", "motif"),
  label = package,
  colors = list(),
  motif_x = 0.5,
  motif_y = NULL,
  motif_scale = 1,
  label_y = 0.215,
  label_size = 32,
  border_width = 5.5,
  shape = c("hex", "pentagon", "square"),
  icon = NULL,
  archive = !missing(package)
)

    Arguments

    package

    Exact identity from hex_catalog().

    mode

    dark, light, or mono.

    layout

    lockup (name inside), hex (unnamed), or motif (standalone).

    label

    Displayed name, defaulting to the exact identity.

    colors

    Named list of colour-role overrides, for example list(face = "#193E36", rim = "#009E73", ink = "white"). Use hex_palette() to see available roles.

    motif_x, motif_y

    Motif centre in normalised canvas coordinates.

    motif_scale

    Motif size multiplier.

    label_y

    Name centre in normalised canvas coordinates.

    label_size

    Maximum name size in points on the six-inch master.

    border_width

    Border width on the six-inch master.

    shape

    Frame shape: hex, pentagon, or square.

    icon

    Optional generic icon key from hexmakr_icons(), replacing the CTTIR motif.

    archive

    Include the package's archive motif. By default this is true only when package is supplied explicitly.

    Value

    A serialisable hex_design object.

    Examples

    design <- hex_design("phenoscapR")
design
